    $$\frac{S_{mod}(M)}{M} = \frac{(M-1)^2 - 1}{2}$$
    $$S_{mod}(M) = \frac{M((M-1)^2 - 1)}{2}$$

2.  **Case 1: $N+1 = M = p$ (Prime)**

    $$\sum_{b=1}^{p-1} (ab \bmod p) = \sum_{k=1}^{p-1} k = \frac{(p-1)p}{2}$$
    Since there are $p-1$ choices for $a$:
